# SPE Round r01 Plan: Ticket Triage Agent

## Headline prediction

No configuration will pass every requirement in r01. All four configurations will miss the P1 recall target of 0.95. The few-shot small model (C2) will score best on accuracy per dollar, but it will cost more than the $2.00 per 1,000 tickets ceiling.

## 0. Before any work

- I will confirm that pwd, the git remote, and the current branch match this repository.
- I will create the `spe/` tree and the files listed in the SPE layout.
- Commits stay local. I will not push. Commit messages carry no attribution lines.

## 1. Specify

The user's prompt is the spec. I will save it verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md`.

The prompt says "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." Nothing exists yet, so I turned that sentence into the task below. Each choice I made is a logged default in section 1.3.

### 1.1 Task definition (default D2)

The agent reads one support ticket. The ticket has a subject, a body, and a customer plan tier. The agent returns JSON with four fields:

```json
{ "category": "bug", "priority": "P2", "reason": "Customer reports export button returns error 500 since Monday." }
```

### 1.2 Requirement table r01

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Return JSON that matches the triage schema for every ticket | D2 | Code: JSON schema validator. Pass if valid rate is at least 0.99 |
| R2 | Pick the correct category | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code: exact match against gold labels. Pass if accuracy is at least 0.85 |
| R3 | Pick the correct priority | User: "triage tickets correctly" | Code: exact match against gold. Pass if accuracy is at least 0.75. Off-by-one rate is reported but not graded |
| R4 | Do not miss P1 tickets | User: "correctly", plus D4 | Code: P1 recall. Pass if at least 0.95 |
| R5 | Keep cost at or below $2.00 per 1,000 tickets | User: "cheaply", plus D5 | Code: API usage tokens times the pinned price table |
| R6 | Keep p95 latency at or below 10 seconds per ticket | D6 | Code: timestamps around each call |
| R7 | Give the same answer to the same ticket across repeats | D7 | Code: share of tickets where all repeats agree on category and priority. Pass if at least 0.90 |
| R8 | The reason field cites something that is in the ticket | D8 | Judge: one model judge per output. Pass if at least 0.90. This is the only judged check |

### 1.3 Disagreements and logged defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I will use | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Where the tickets come from | A separate agent writes 120 synthetic tickets with gold labels from a written product brief. Real anonymized tickets would test the agent better | User | Open. Default logged |
| D2 | Output schema | category, priority, reason, as shown in 1.1 | Claude | Default |
| D3 | Category list and priority rules | Seven categories: billing, bug, outage, account_access, feature_request, how_to, spam. P1 means service down, data loss, or a security issue. P2 means a core feature is broken for one customer. P3 means a minor issue or a question with a workaround. P4 means a request or spam | User | Open. Default logged |
| D4 | Which error is worse | Missing a P1 is worse than over-calling one. R4 grades recall only | User | Open. Default logged |
| D5 | Cost ceiling | $2.00 per 1,000 tickets | User | Open. Default logged |
| D6 | Latency ceiling | p95 of 10 seconds | Claude | Default |
| D7 | Agent shape in r01 | One model call with schema-enforced output and no tools | Claude | Default |
| D8 | Model tiers | One small tier and one mid tier from the current Anthropic lineup. I will pin exact model IDs and prices from current docs at build time and write them to the price table before the run | Claude | Default. Verify at build |
| D9 | Language | Node.js, the same as the Workflow script | Claude | Default |
| D10 | Trust in gold labels | A blind relabel of 20 test tickets must agree at least 85% of the time, or the round halts | Claude | Default |

## 2. Predict

### 2.1 Configurations

Each configuration changes one thing from its parent.

| Config | What it is | Parent | The one change |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | Keyword rules, no model | none | Baseline |
| C1 | Small tier model, zero-shot, schema-enforced | C0 | Rules replaced by the small model |
| C2 | C1 plus 6 few-shot examples from the dev split | C1 | Adds few-shot examples |
| C3 | Mid tier model, zero-shot, same prompt as C1 | C1 | Larger model |

### 2.2 Prediction table

This is round 1, so no "same as last round" values exist. The naive guess I will score against is "C2 and C3 score the same as C1."

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | C3 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 | 0.99 | 1.00 | 1.00 | R1 schema validator | Rules emit fixed JSON. Schema-enforced model output rarely fails, and examples remove the rare failure |
| Category accuracy | 0.55 | 0.82 | 0.87 | 0.88 | R2 exact match | Keywords miss paraphrased tickets. Few-shot examples fix bug versus outage confusion. The mid model gains a little on ambiguous tickets |
| Priority accuracy | 0.45 | 0.65 | 0.72 | 0.74 | R3 exact match | Priority depends on impact and plan tier rules, and zero-shot models apply those loosely |
| P1 recall | 0.60 | 0.85 | 0.90 | 0.92 | R4 recall | Models under-call P1 when a ticket is written in a calm tone |
| Cost per 1,000 tickets (USD) | 0.00 | 1.10 | 2.60 | 3.30 | R5 token cost | About 800 input and 60 output tokens per call. Few-shot adds about 1,500 input tokens. The mid tier costs about 3 times as much per token. Prices are estimates until pinned |
| p95 latency (seconds) | 0.01 | 2.5 | 3.0 | 4.5 | R6 timestamps | Short output keeps calls fast. The longer prompt and the larger model add time |
| Repeat consistency | 1.00 | 0.93 | 0.95 | 0.95 | R7 repeat agreement | Rules are deterministic. Examples anchor the model on borderline tickets |
| Reason cites ticket | 0.90 | 0.95 | 0.96 | 0.97 | R8 judge | C0 reasons name the matched keyword. That passes unless the keyword is generic |
| Requirements passed (of 8) | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | Count of R1 to R8 | C0 and C1 fail R2, R3, R4. C2 and C3 fail R3, R4, R5 |

## 3. Evaluate

### 3.1 Data

- The generator agent writes 120 tickets and their gold labels before any builder sees the data.
- 40 tickets form the dev split. 80 tickets form the test split, with at least 12 P1 tickets.
- Ticket text lives in `spe/evals/data/tickets/`. Gold labels live in `spe/evals/data/gold/`. Only the grader reads the gold folder.

### 3.2 Build steps

| Step | What happens | Who sees what |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Generator agent writes the tickets and gold labels from the D3 rules | Sees the product brief and D3 only |
| H2 | Builder agent writes `src/triage/` with the rules baseline, prompt, schema, and config loader | Sees the dev split only |
| H3 | I write `spe/evals/harness/grade.js` with code checks for R1 to R7 and one judge for R8 | Reads gold |
| H4 | I pin model IDs and prices from current docs into `spe/evals/harness/prices.json` | None |
| H5 | I write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. It holds `const ROUND = "r01"`, and every prompt reads the round from it | None |

### 3.3 Gates before launch

| Gate | Check | Halt if |
|---|---|---|
| G1 Grader selftest | The oracle (gold copied as answers) scores 1.00. Empty output fails R1. Shuffled labels score near chance | Any of the three is wrong |
| G2 Label check | A fresh agent labels 20 test tickets blind | Agreement is below 0.85 |
| G3 Control | r01 has no prior round to regrade. I run C0 twice on the test split instead and require identical scores. Round r02 will regrade r01 as its control | Scores differ |
| G4 Dry run | 3 cells: C0 on ticket 1, C1 on ticket 2, C3 on ticket 3. I check the schema, cost logging, and transcripts | Any cell errors or logs no cost |
| G5 Budget | Projected spend is under the caps in 3.4 | Projection crosses a cap |

### 3.4 Workflow run

```
ROUND:              "r01"
configs:            [C0, C1, C2, C3]
test_set:           spe/evals/data/tickets/test/
gold (grader only): spe/evals/data/gold/
repeats:            3
extra_repeats_cap:  60 calls total
max_output_tokens:  200
concurrency:        8
api_budget_usd_cap: 10.00
subagent_model:     Opus
subagent_cap:       8 agents, 40 turns each
```

- The run covers 4 configs times 80 tickets times 3 repeats, which is 960 trials. 720 of them are paid model calls.
- A split cell is a ticket and config pair where repeats disagree. Split cells get up to 2 extra repeats until the 60-call cap is reached.
- The harness skips any trial that would cross a cap and logs the skip.
- The triage call receives the ticket text only.
- A leak scan reads the builder and trial transcripts for any path under `gold/`, `grader`, `predictions/`, or the test split. The scan voids any trial that peeked and voids the round if the builder read the test split.
- A failure analysis agent groups every miss into F-numbered failure types.
- A completeness critic checks that every requirement and every prediction cell has a measured number, and that every skip is logged.

### 3.5 Cost estimate (unmeasured)

| Item | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Triage calls (720 plus up to 60 extra) | About $2 |
| R8 judge calls | About $3 |
| Dataset generation and label check | About $1 |
| Workflow subagents for build, analysis, and critic | $10 to $20 |
| Total | $16 to $26 |

These figures are estimates. I will replace them with measured spend at close-out.

## 4. After approval

1. Write the transcript, `spec.md`, and `disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify: triage spec from prompt, 8 requirements, 10 defaults`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with the header `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.`, the round, the date, the author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its Why, the naive guess, and `same_as_last_round: null`. Commit `SPE r01 predict: no config passes all, P1 recall is the blocker`.
3. Build H1 to H5 and pass gates G1 to G5. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. It returns at launch. I will close out when the completion notice arrives.
5. Commit the raw results and grades as `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
6. Learn:
   - Write `spe/prediction-log.md` with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, a "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. It also states whether the naive guess beat my predictions.
   - Write `spe/failures.md` with one entry per new failure type. Each entry has a name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure, and original and regraded numbers sit side by side.
   - Add a "Proposed for round 2" table to `spec.md` and write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
   - Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r01`.

I will never edit `r01.yaml` after the first trial runs.

## 5. Halt and stop rules

- I will halt and report if a budget cap is hit, the answer key leaks, a gate fails, or a decision needs the user.
- If every configuration passes everything, round 2 needs harder tickets or stricter graders.
- The loop stops when predictions match results for 3 rounds in a row.
